title: Minimax Allocation of One Noncase Assay after Observing Subgroup Case Counts
banked_reason: Delivered tier incremental < floor field; not salvageable within scope. Mathematical soundness not established: two undeclared proof dependencies and one related-work omission remain unrepaired after D0.5 novelty triage.
gap_reasons: Delivered tier incremental < floor field; not salvageable within scope.

The note proves exact unrestricted minimax equalities and a strict risk gap only for a highly specialized two-equal-stratum Poisson experiment with known intensity near one and exactly one additional noncase assay.
The finite-cohort theorem supplies a two-sided O(1/N) risk comparison, not an attained finite-N minimax characterization.

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery drafted exact unrestricted Poisson minimax equalities, a connected-class endpoint envelope, a strict post-count risk gap, and uniform O(1/N) finite-cohort transfer. D0.5 judged the delivered package incremental and not salvageable at the fixed field floor: exact finite-N minimax would require a new saddle-point proof for a different observation kernel. Novelty triage stopped before two undeclared proof dependencies and a related-work omission were repaired, so mathematical soundness is not established; no Lean formalization was attempted.
tldr: A two-stratum rare-outcome cohort observes every subgroup label and case status, assays all cases, and has a budget for one additional noncase assay. The core asks for exact minimax risks when the assay stratum is fixed in advance or selected after subgroup case counts, but before exposure marks; in a finite cohort an empty selected noncase pool produces an explicit no-assay observation and a measurable fallback action. A four-point opposite-corner prior supplies unrestricted Bayes lower bounds under the post-allocation assay kernel, while an analytic curvature argument and a cutoff-twelve exact rational certificate extend the matching upper risks to the full connected prevalence class. The resulting strict gain is certified between \(7758/10^6\) and \(7759/10^6\), transfers uniformly to finite cohorts through two explicit Markov kernels with a common augmented codomain, and exposes an open intensity frontier defined by primitive saddle inequalities.
gap: Published two-phase allocation theory optimizes regular asymptotic efficiency or model-based design criteria. It does not determine the finite-Poisson, all-estimator squared-risk value of observing subgroup case counts before allocating one noncase assay, and a symmetric finite-family calculation does not justify extension to a connected probability class.
fill: The project pairs an unrestricted corner-prior Bayes lower bound with an attaining posterior rule, analytic convexity in case-exposure prevalence, exact rational interval curvature in exposure prevalence, and two common-codomain Markov-kernel comparisons for finite-cohort transfer. It also defines the intensity frontier by explicit least-favorable-prior and attaining-rule saddle predicates.
